question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual total of number_of_motorist_killed, including every recorded motorist death associated with eligible crashes
options.denominator: None; this is a count, not a rate
options.reason: Annual fatality counts provide a direct and easily interpreted description of the recorded toll, while making no unsupported exposure adjustment.
options.answer: Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but these counts cannot show whether deaths per mile driven declined.
options.interpretation: Using all police-reported NYC crash rows dated 2013–2025, grouped by crash year, this chart sums number_of_motorist_killed and shows the recorded death count falling from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, with 139 in 2020. Annual counts are a defensible way to describe the recorded toll, but they are not an exposure-adjusted risk measure. The file has no miles-driven denominator, so this framing cannot answer whether deaths per mile declined. The check covers 2,132,218 rows, with 0 missing dates and 0 missing motorist-death values; all rows were retained, including the 381 (0.018%) dated 2013-01-01 because the check did not establish those dates as defaults, and observed endpoints span every year.

options.metric: Crashes with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero per 1,000 eligible crashes
options.denominator: All police-reported NYC crash rows in the same calendar year
options.reason: A crash-denominated ratio adjusts for changes in the number of reported crashes and offers a defensible, though non-mile-based, comparison over time.
options.answer: Motorist-fatality crashes rose from 0.501 to 0.877 per 1,000 reported crashes between 2013 and 2025, so this crash-based measure did not decline; it cannot establish the per-mile trend.
options.interpretation: For all police-reported NYC crash rows dated 2013–2025, grouped by crash year, the chart counts rows with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero and divides by all crash rows in that year, reporting the result per 1,000 crashes. This crash-normalized proxy rose from 0.501 per 1,000 in 2013 to 0.877 in 2025, although it is not a count of individual deaths or a per-mile risk measure. The file has no miles-driven denominator, so it cannot answer whether deaths per mile declined. answer:
Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but this unadjusted count cannot show whether deaths per mile driven declined ([chart](out/option_1.png)).
Motorist-fatality crashes rose from 0.501 to 0.877 per 1,000 reported crashes over the same period, but this crash-based measure cannot establish the per-mile trend ([chart](out/option_2.png)).
